title: The Holy Grail of Baseball Cards Is Up for Auction
summary:
One of the most famous baseball cards in history is up for auction. Bidding has already passed $1 million, and there are still days left to go.

The card shows Honus Wagner and was made between 1909 and 1911. Its full official name is very long, but Heritage Auctions has a simpler nickname for it: the Holy Grail of baseball cards. A holy grail is something that people search for and want very badly.

Chris Ivy, who leads sports auctions at Heritage, called the T206 Wagner card the foundational trophy of baseball card collecting.

Honus Wagner is still one of baseball's most respected players. He was the son of a German immigrant who worked as a coal miner. Wagner, nicknamed the Flying Dutchman, played shortstop for the Pittsburgh Pirates from 1900 to 1917. He won eight batting titles. In 1937, he became one of the first players chosen for the Baseball Hall of Fame in Cooperstown, New York.

So why is his card so rare? Long ago, collectible cards came with tobacco products. Legend says Wagner told the company to stop printing cards with his picture after learning they were being used to sell cigarettes. Because so few of his cards were made, collectors want them very much.

This card is only the sixth T206 Wagner ever sold by Heritage Auctions. The bid stood at $1,025,000, and bidding runs until October 25. The sellers expect the card to sell for at least $3 million.

That might sound like a lot, but earlier this year, a similar Honus Wagner card from the same years sold for more than $5.8 million.
why_it_matters: The card shows how a small piece of sports history can become hugely valuable when it is rare and tied to a legendary player.

background_read: Baseball cards are small printed cards showing players, and people have collected and traded them for more than a century.
A card's value depends on how rare it is, how famous the player is and what condition the card is in.
At an auction, buyers place higher and higher bids until time runs out, and the highest bidder wins the item.
Honus Wagner's cards from the early 1900s are especially rare because very few were printed, which is why collectors prize them so much.
